messages.author: 8f656b07cc1ee6a5
messages.subject: incomplete last line warning on Azure ?
parts:
I transferred my good ( for a newbie ) run of a model with RStan  from my I7 laptio onto a windows VM on Azure ( Microsoft's cloud ) , On the Azure VM,  I installed R and Rstan and Rstudio as accurately as possible, no errors that I saw. I then transferred my application code and data - as exactly as possible to the best of my knowledge. As a matter of rote I did a IVP / regression test, running the model with the same seed on Azure  as on my laptop - but printing the coeffs I saw they were quite different. For the moment, I can't at all get a handle on this. I get this message on AZURE 

Chain 1, Iteration: 5000 / 5000 [100%]  (Sampling)
 Elapsed Time: 1177.76 seconds (Warm-up)
               1284.36 seconds (Sampling)
               2462.12 seconds (Total)

Warning message:
In readLines(file, warn = TRUE) :
  incomplete final line found on 'C:\AllSessMktMix\stan\SEOModel_AllSpends.stan'

Its coming from somewhere in RSTAN right ? Ideas please ? Stackoverflow suggests issues like  changing encoding in read.table argument from fileEncoding = "UTF-16" to fileEncoding = "UTF-8".

O I've dummy edited the file on Azure to try and reset its End of File marker and that sort of stuff.. I think this issue is important at that cos as I said, the results in the two environments, with the same seed are rather different. One final thing.. you know how at the end of a print the object you normally get a "your fit is .8, .9 etc".. On Azure I don't get it.. All I get is this, nothing more. 

Samples were drawn using NUTS2 at Fri Apr 12 22:09:54 2013.
For each parameter, n_eff is a crude measure of effective sample size,
and Rhat is the potential scale reduction factor on split chains (at 
convergence, Rhat=1).

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] incomplete last line warning on Azure ?
parts:
There's no guarantee you'll get the same results across
different hardware/compilers/operating systems.

Can you just call readLines() on the same file? I don't
think RStan's doing anything fancy with the encodings.

Maybe the RStan devs will have more insight. It'll probably
help if they can see your sessionInfo() from R to see what
else is installed and see which C++ compiler you're using.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] incomplete last line warning on Azure ?
parts:
On Saturday, August 6, 2016 at 8:27:35 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
Can you just call readLines() on the same file?  I don't
think RStan's doing anything fancy with the encodings.

Stan programs should end with a blank line after the final }. Otherwise, rstan will try to recompile them even if they have not changed on disk.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: incomplete last line warning on Azure ?
parts:
So I switched to the 8schools example to test this further, so that it can be repeated elsewhere. Using the 8schools code then:

Summary.
1. Indeed the last line warning disappears if I add a blank line to the end of the file. There is no incomplete line warning either if I use the model_code parameter to specify the model as a R character string, rather than a text file. Also the results are the same on Azure where I use the model_code argument or when I use a file and get a incomplete last line warning. So that doesn't seem to affect the results then.

But I noticed on Azure my stan version is 2.11.0 whereas on my PC it is 2.10.0 and since I didn't get the warning on my PC, I think there may be some changes in 2.11.0 ( or on my Azure environment ) as well that cause the incomplete line warning.

2. Totally since the stan versions differ between my PC and the AZURE vm I get different results despite the same seed. The results from the two versions are attached. To really eliminate AZURE from the equation I wanted to load  and use stan V2.10.0  in the AZURE vm, but I can't find it in the cran repositories as a windows BINARY or source at all.... I can find 2.10.1 as a source but well.. for an apples to apples comparison the 2.10.0 binary would be best.

Anywhere else I shd look to get the windows binary for stan 2.10.0. ?

Stan doesn't have reproducible results across versions or
across hardware/compiler/operating system. There's a chapter
in the manual on what you need for reproduciblity, but it's
basically *everything that can be nailed down must be*.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] incomplete last line warning on Azure ?
parts:
Because MCMC is a probabilistic process, we need
probabilistic tests. But 2.10 wasn't just different,
there was a bug, which meant it got the *wrong* answers.
The bugs are hard to catch given the probabilistic nature
of the process and not wanting the tests to take too
long wall time (which means they don't get run or hold
everything up) or emit false positives (which means we'd
ignore them).

- Bob
